uncited: NeRF Optimization refers to the process of training a continuous volumetric scene representation, typically parameterized by a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), to predict density and color from 3D coordinates and viewing directions .
It solves the problem of novel view synthesis by learning a differentiable volume rendering function that maps camera parameters to pixel colors via ray marching .

It sets itself apart from discrete mesh-based rendering by modeling geometry as a continuous density field, allowing for high-fidelity reconstruction of complex, unstructured scenes without explicit topology .
All methods in this family aim to maintain visual fidelity while reducing the total number of volume queries .
NeRF was introduced by Mildenhall et al. in 2020 .
The method represents a scene as a continuous 5D function mapping $(x, y, z, \theta, \phi)$ to volume density and view-dependent color.
Optimization involves minimizing the photometric loss between rendered images and ground-truth views using stochastic gradient descent.
The foundational approach uses uniform sampling along rays, which is computationally expensive.
Subsequent works have focused on acceleration through adaptive sampling, hierarchical representations, and alternative optimization objectives like Score Distillation Sampling .
